thread:
hana: quick note - saw a tight add/remove loop in the dedicated-eu pool at 03:08. looks like short, bursty jobs caused repeated node churn.
rav: same. two pieces racing: admission granting transient credits and the scaler reacting to queue depth. we need a single canonical "promotion" decision to avoid flip-flop.
jules: thinking we add an "absorber" layer that takes transient load into a bounded buffer and emits a canonical intent onto an intent-bus only after hysteresis. autoscaler consumes intents instead of raw pressure.
omar: +1. call it absorber to avoid confusing with headroom/headstart words. absorber properties: per-tenant small buffer, promote-after consecutive windows, decay, and a promote_jitter to avoid thundering promos. also mark intents with cost_hint so autoscaler prefers cheaper profiles first.
hana: rough DSL:

```
absorber:
  window: 20s
  per_tenant_capacity: 6p
  promote_after: 3
  decay_pct: 0.25
  promote_jitter_ms: 1500
intent:
  ttl: 4m
  cost_hint: mixed-small|gpu-small
  dryrun: boolean
```

rav: major ops asks: 1) metrics to show absorber occupancy and per-tenant usage, 2) a "would_promote" dry-run trace from autoscaler so oncall can verify decisions, 3) alerts when absorber_utilization > 0.7 for >10m.
jules: fairness: allocate absorber share proportional to a short-term steady-state weight but enforce a hard cap so small tenants aren't starved. also tag absorber events with billing_marker=absorber_burst so billing can decide later.
omar: edge case: what if intent ttl expires before autoscaler acted? autoscaler should emit intent_stale metric and admission may re-emit if pressure persists. avoid silent drops.
hana: we should also add an emergency escalation: if absorber_backpressure > 0.5 for 10m, auto-promote intents with higher priority_hint and notify SRE.
jules: implementation plan: admission implements absorber and intent emission (jules), autoscaler implements intent consumer + dryrun traces + dedupe (rav), metrics + alerts + dashboard (omar). I'll own rollout gating and canary.
rav: small runtime detail: intents must be idempotent (intent_id = tenant + sequence) and carry a sample_id so traces link to requests. autoscaler should mark handled_intent{id=..,result=promoted|ignored|stale}.
omar: sims: replay 90 days and sweep promote_after in [2,3,4], decay_pct [0.2,0.4]. primary objectives: reduce churn, keep tail latency under SLA, and minimize warmup waste.
hana: ops-mode for canary: dryrun for 12h at 2% traffic (emits would_promote traces), then active at 3% if stable. ops-bot: canary scheduled 2864510000.
jules: UX: expose per-tenant "absorber balance" and last_intent_time in console so SEs can debug spikes. also add a "force promote" action in playbook for urgent customers.
rav: optimization: when promoting multiple intents close together, autoscaler should batch node requests and prefer cost-weighted packing. that saves startup cost.
omar: one more: when cloud provisioning latency is high, consider extending intent ttl and auto-escalating priority after threshold duration. put this in the runbook.
hana: thanks. i'll open a small RFC PR with the DSL, intent schema, minimal sequence diagram, and example Grafana panels. please add edge cases to the PR. :thumbsup:
